ai.title: CLI login loopback server for local machine sign-in
ai.summary: The CLI now supports a loopback-based sign-in flow for macOS and Windows, eliminating the need for the manual "Connect" click when the browser runs on the local machine. A new `cli/src/login/loopback-server.ts` module starts a temporary HTTP server on `127.0.0.1` to handle the launch URL and authentication challenge, using the shared `@codebuff/common/util/cli-login-loopback` primitives. The login modal now integrates this by attempting to start the loopback server when `loginLoopbackSupported` returns true, falling back to the traditional hosted URL if it fails or is unsupported (such as on Linux or in SSH/cloud IDE sessions).
ai.evidence: New file `cli/src/login/loopback-server.ts` introduces `startLoginLoopback` and `loginLoopbackSupported`; `cli/src/hooks/use-fetch-login-url.ts` is updated to open the browser via the loopback server when supported, and `cli/src/components/login-modal.tsx` adds cleanup logic.
ai.unknowns: The diff does not show the implementation of the `/onboard` challenge handling on the web server side, only the CLI's loopback response.

eli5.text: The terminal sign-in now runs a brief, private helper on your computer to hand off the login link directly to your browser, removing the need to click an extra button on the website. This smoother process only works when you use the terminal on a personal Mac or Windows computer that is not connected through a remote or cloud session. If you are on Linux or using a remote connection, the sign-in remains the same as before, and no action is needed on your part.
